gap: No result ChatGPT got states how long a 4-channel dash cam records before it starts overwriting footage. Using DashCamTalk's bitrates, all four channels together write about 21 GB per hour: 128 GB holds about 6 hours on the REDTIGER F17 Plus (46 Mbps, 128 GB card in the box) and about 5.9 hours on the Vantrue N5S (48.2 Mbps).
standout_why: Dashlore's best-dash-cams guide lists the N5S's resolutions and its 1,024 GB maximum card but gives no bitrate, no hours per card and no storage per hour. Mydrivecar's 4-channel list gives included and maximum card sizes for six cameras but, by its own tables, no bitrate or recording hours. Car and Driver, the cited page, could not be fetched (the tool is blocked from caranddriver.com), so I could not check it. Our current page gives no recording hours either.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. The F17 Plus ($199.99) and the N5S ($293.99) fill a 128 GB card in about the same 6 hours, so storage does not separate them. Either way, a shopper who wants a full day of 4-channel loop needs a card of 256 GB or more: about 11.8 h on the N5S. Only the N5S is sourced to take 1 TB, about 46 h. A related point for this question: DashCamTalk lists the F17 Plus's channels as Front, Rear, Interior and Interior Rear, and REDTIGER's own listing calls it a 'dual cabin lens'. So ChatGPT's 'top pick for side coverage' has no exterior left or right camera, the same limit it flagged on the N5S.
